description: Local industrial knowledge taxonomy for MEDHA. Terminology, categories, synonyms and abbreviations used to normalise industrial language, expand retrieval queries, and tag extracted document content. Fully offline - no external ontology service.

categories.process_unit: Named process units inside a refinery or petrochemical complex

abbreviations.FMECA: Failure Mode, Effects and Criticality Analysis

refinery.definition: Industrial facility that separates and converts crude oil into fuels, lubricants and petrochemical feedstocks.

petrochemical plant.definition: Facility converting refinery or gas streams into chemical intermediates and polymers.

crude distillation unit.definition: Primary refinery unit separating crude oil into fractions by boiling range at near-atmospheric pressure.

vacuum distillation unit.definition: Unit distilling atmospheric residue under vacuum to recover gas oils without thermal cracking.

fluid catalytic cracking.definition: Conversion process cracking heavy gas oils into gasoline and light olefins over a fluidised zeolite catalyst.

hydrotreater.definition: Unit removing sulphur, nitrogen and metals from hydrocarbon streams by reaction with hydrogen over a catalyst.

hydrocracker.definition: High-pressure unit cracking heavy feed into lighter products in the presence of hydrogen and a dual-function catalyst.

reformer.definition: Catalytic unit upgrading naphtha to high-octane reformate and hydrogen; also refers to a steam reformer producing hydrogen from natural gas.

hydrogen unit.definition: Unit producing hydrogen, typically by steam methane reforming with pressure-swing adsorption purification.

sulphur recovery unit.definition: Unit converting hydrogen sulphide from amine and sour water systems into elemental sulphur, usually by the Claus process.

boiler.definition: Fired or waste-heat pressure vessel generating steam from boiler feed water.

cooling tower.definition: Evaporative heat rejection device that cools circulating water for plant heat exchangers.

pump.definition: Machine adding energy to a liquid to raise its pressure or move it through a system.

compressor.definition: Machine raising the pressure of a gas; centrifugal, reciprocating or screw type in process plants.

turbine.definition: Machine extracting shaft work from a flowing fluid; steam and gas turbines drive generators and large compressors.

motor.definition: Electrical machine converting electrical power into rotating mechanical power to drive pumps, fans and compressors.

heat exchanger.definition: Equipment transferring heat between two fluids without mixing them; shell-and-tube, plate or air-cooled.

pressure vessel.definition: Closed container designed to hold gases or liquids at a pressure different from ambient, designed to a code such as ASME VIII.

storage tank.definition: Atmospheric or low-pressure tank storing crude, intermediates or products; typically designed to API 650 and inspected to API 653.

distillation column.definition: Vertical vessel separating a mixture into fractions by repeated vapour-liquid contact on trays or packing.

fired heater.definition: Direct-fired equipment heating process fluid in tubes inside a combustion chamber.

pipeline.definition: Long-distance pipe system transporting crude, products, gas or utilities between facilities.

piping.definition: In-plant pipe, fittings and supports carrying process and utility fluids; designed to codes such as ASME B31.3.

valve.definition: Device controlling flow direction, rate or pressure in a piping system.

actuator.definition: Pneumatic, hydraulic, electric or manual device that moves a valve to its commanded position.

relief valve.definition: Self-actuated safety device that opens at set pressure to protect equipment from overpressure.

control loop.definition: Closed-loop arrangement of measurement, controller and final element that holds a process variable at setpoint.

plc.definition: Industrial digital controller executing cyclic logic for discrete and sequential control.

dcs.definition: Distributed Control System: plant-wide control architecture with distributed controllers and centralised operator consoles.

scada.definition: Supervisory system collecting telemetry and issuing commands across geographically distributed assets.

safety instrumented system.definition: Independent instrumented protection layer that takes the process to a safe state when defined limits are exceeded.

instrumentation.definition: Field devices that measure, indicate, transmit and act on process variables.

transmitter.definition: Instrument converting a measured process variable into a standard signal (4-20 mA, HART, fieldbus).

vibration.definition: Oscillatory motion of machinery, measured as displacement, velocity or acceleration and used as the primary indicator of rotating-machine health.

temperature.definition: Measured thermal state of a process, bearing or surface; a primary process and condition variable.

pressure.definition: Force per unit area exerted by a fluid; measured for control, protection and integrity assessment.

flow.definition: Volumetric or mass rate of fluid movement, measured for control, balance and custody transfer.

level.definition: Height of liquid or interface in a vessel or tank; a key control and safety variable.

corrosion.definition: Degradation of material by chemical or electrochemical reaction with its environment.

damage mechanism.definition: Specific degradation process acting on equipment, such as sulphidation, HTHA, chloride stress corrosion cracking or creep.

inspection.definition: Planned examination of equipment condition to confirm fitness for service and detect degradation.

non-destructive testing.definition: Techniques that examine material condition without impairing usefulness - UT, RT, MPI, PT, ECT and visual methods.

thickness measurement.definition: Ultrasonic or radiographic measurement of remaining wall thickness at defined monitoring locations.

preventive maintenance.definition: Maintenance performed at fixed intervals of time or usage to reduce the probability of failure.

predictive maintenance.definition: Maintenance triggered by measured or modelled equipment condition rather than a fixed calendar interval.

condition monitoring.definition: Continuous or periodic measurement of machine and equipment parameters to detect developing faults.

maintenance strategy.definition: The chosen mix of corrective, preventive, predictive and redesign tactics for an asset, usually selected via RCM.

work order.definition: Formal instruction authorising and recording a maintenance job, its resources, permits and completion notes.

turnaround.definition: Planned, plant-wide shutdown for inspection, maintenance and modification of equipment that cannot be serviced online.

shutdown.definition: Controlled or automatic stopping of a unit or equipment item, planned or triggered by protection systems.

startup.definition: Sequence bringing a unit from a shutdown state to stable operating conditions.

permit to work.definition: Formal written authorisation controlling hazardous work, defining precautions, isolation and validity period.

lockout/tagout.definition: Procedure isolating and locking energy sources, with tags identifying the isolation, before work begins.

process safety.definition: Discipline preventing loss of containment and major accidents through design, procedures and protection layers.

hazop.definition: Structured team review applying guidewords to process deviations to identify hazards and operability problems.

risk assessment.definition: Systematic evaluation of hazard likelihood and consequence to decide whether risk is tolerable and what controls are needed.

emergency response.definition: Planned organisation and procedures for responding to fires, releases, injuries and other plant emergencies.

incident.definition: Unplanned event that caused or could have caused injury, loss of containment, damage or business interruption.

failure mode.definition: The specific way in which an item fails to perform its required function.

root cause.definition: The underlying condition or decision whose correction prevents recurrence of a failure.

reliability.definition: Probability that an item performs its required function under stated conditions for a stated period.

availability.definition: Proportion of time an asset is capable of performing its function, combining reliability and maintainability.

calibration.definition: Comparison of an instrument's output against a traceable reference and adjustment to bring error within tolerance.

engineering standard.definition: Published technical requirement (API, ASME, ISO, IEC, ISA, OISD, IBR) governing design, inspection or operation.

p&id.definition: Piping and Instrumentation Diagram: schematic showing equipment, piping, instruments and control functions with tag numbers.

datasheet.definition: Document listing the design, construction and performance data of an equipment item or instrument.

standard operating procedure.definition: Approved step-by-step instruction for carrying out an operating or maintenance task safely and consistently.

shift log.definition: Chronological record of plant conditions, actions, abnormalities and handover notes kept by operating shifts.

equipment_tag_patterns.description: Regex fragments used to spot equipment tag numbers in extracted text. Prefix letters follow common refinery conventions.

claim_types.historical_fact: Dated, verifiable event or development from the industrial history corpus.
claim_types.engineering_principle: General physical or engineering principle that is not site-specific.
claim_types.modern_best_practice: Current industry practice or recommended approach, not a mandatory requirement.
claim_types.company_specific: Information specific to one company, plant or organisation.
claim_types.user_document: Content extracted from a document the user supplied.
claim_types.ai_inference: Conclusion produced by the model, not directly present in any source.
